c.tagline: Maritime harbour city of seafood, sea shanties, and Titanic history.

taxi.fareNote: Uber and Lyft both operate in Halifax alongside metered local cabs, and ride-hail is widely available downtown. The airport run is often a flat rate of around C$68.

emergency.note: 911 connects to police, fire, and ambulance across Nova Scotia.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Late-night rowdiness around the downtown bar strip on Argyle and Lower Water streets on weekends warrants basic awareness.

hood_desc: The compact, walkable core running down to the Halifax Waterfront Boardwalk, home to the Maritime Museum of the Atlantic, historic Old Town Clock, breweries, and most seafood restaurants; the easiest base for first-timers who want everything on foot.

A trendy, creative district of Victorian rowhouses, indie coffee shops, craft breweries, and the buzzing Gottingen Street strip, plus the Halifax Seaport Farmers' Market nearby; suits younger travellers wanting local, hip character.
A leafy, upscale residential quarter of grand old homes near Dalhousie University, Point Pleasant Park, and the cruise terminal; a calm, green base a short walk or bus ride from downtown.

A busy shopping and dining street just uphill from the waterfront, lined with boutiques, cafes, and the Halifax Public Gardens; central and lively, good for shoppers who still want to walk everywhere.

The harbour city facing Halifax across the water, reached by a scenic passenger ferry, with its own waterfront, lakes, breweries, and a more laid-back, local feel; a quieter and often cheaper place to stay.
lodging: The Hollis Halifax, a Tapestry Collection by Hilton

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6am-midnight, with some later routes on weekends; the harbour ferries run about 6am-midnight (later on weekends).
transit.note: Halifax Transit runs the city buses and the harbour ferries to Dartmouth; there is no rail or subway system.
transit.pay: Tap a contactless credit/debit card or phone, or use the HFXGO app or a Tap card, on buses and ferries. One adult fare is about C$4.25 and includes 90 minutes of free transfers between buses and the ferry; exact cash fare is also accepted on board.

bus: Maritime Bus terminal (at VIA Rail Halifax Station)
ferry: Halifax Ferry Terminal (harbour ferry to Dartmouth)
train: Halifax Station (VIA Rail Ocean to Montreal)

transit.m: Maritime Bus airport shuttle to downtown (~40 min)
Halifax Transit Route 320 MetroX to downtown (~60 min)

tip.r: 15-20% at restaurants and bars is expected; tip taxis and ride-hail drivers around 10-15%.
